claims.title: Small-subproblem insertion crossover
claims.hypothesis: Insertion sort has a measurable small-n region where low overhead offsets quadratic scaling; the crossover is domain-dependent.
required_evidence: paired uncertainty around insertion vs merge crossover

claims.title: Binary versus linear insertion
claims.hypothesis: Binary insertion trades fewer comparisons for additional control work and can reverse ranking with n, input order, or comparison cost.
required_evidence: paired claim-matrix output across small-n workloads

claims.title: Insertion-leaf hybrids
claims.hypothesis: Merge, median-of-three quicksort, and introsort can improve by switching to insertion sort on sufficiently small leaves; the best cutoff is not universal.
required_evidence: domain-specific cutoff surface or replicated scoped default

claims.title: Duplicate-aware partitioning
claims.hypothesis: Three-way quicksort becomes more favorable as duplicate entropy falls.

claims.title: Radix digit width
claims.hypothesis: Wider radix digits trade fewer passes against larger histogram/cache footprint, causing architecture- and size-dependent crossover behavior.
required_evidence: Linux hardware campaign when making cache-mechanism claims

claims.title: Run adaptivity
claims.hypothesis: Natural/run-adaptive merging benefits sufficiently structured inputs but may pay overhead on structureless data.
required_evidence: paired natural vs fixed merge effects

claims.title: Heap mechanism
claims.hypothesis: Heapsort wall-time behavior can be worse than comparison counts imply because locality/branch behavior differs from alternatives.
required_evidence: direct hardware counters for any causal mechanism statement

claims.title: Record width
claims.hypothesis: Increasing record width changes rankings as whole-record movement becomes more expensive.
required_evidence: record-core across all preregistered payload widths

claims.title: Cost of stability
claims.hypothesis: The cost of stability varies with duplicates, record width, n, and implementation.

claims.title: No universal winner
claims.hypothesis: Algorithm rankings and crossover points vary with workload, type, and environment.
required_evidence: at least two materially different Tier-3 environments before cross-machine conclusion

claims.title: Feature-based portfolio
claims.hypothesis: A cheap runtime input probe may improve held-out performance by choosing among complementary algorithms after paying probe overhead.
required_evidence: comparison to training-selected best fixed algorithm
oracle regret reported only as an upper-bound reference

claims.title: Tiny-kernel crossover
claims.hypothesis: A data-oblivious bitonic network can outperform insertion sort in some small-array domains, while adaptive insertion can remain superior on sufficiently ordered inputs; crossover points are environment-dependent.
required_evidence: paired bootstrap uncertainty versus insertion for each n/workload cell
cross-environment replication before universal threshold claims

claims.title: Leaf-kernel integration effect
claims.hypothesis: A tiny sorter that wins in isolation may not be the best base case inside merge, quick, or introsort because integration changes code-footprint and execution-context costs.
required_evidence: kernel and cutoff selected on training trials only
held-out comparison against best training-selected insertion-only cutoff
direct hardware evidence for any branch/cache mechanism claim

claims.title: Adaptive merge scheduling
claims.hypothesis: For skewed natural-run distributions, merge schedule materially changes weighted merge cost; Powersort should often reduce redundancy relative to naive pairwise scheduling and can differ from the repaired TimSort stack policy, without implying universal wall-time dominance.
required_evidence: exact alphabetic merge-cost model on preregistered run-length sequences
paired wall-time uncertainty with a common merge kernel

claims.title: Balanced minrun scheduling
claims.hypothesis: A variable balanced minrun sequence can reduce run-size imbalance and merge-tree redundancy on short-run inputs relative to a fixed classic minrun, but the wall-time effect depends on n, input structure, and insertion-extension cost.
required_evidence: same merge policy compared across classic and balanced minrun treatments

claims.title: Smaller-run merge buffering
claims.hypothesis: Buffering only the smaller adjacent run strictly reduces requested temporary workspace for each merge and may improve data movement or locality, while forward/backward merge asymmetry can make wall-time effects domain-dependent.
required_evidence: same search policy compared across full and smaller-run buffers
direct hardware evidence for any cache or bandwidth mechanism claim

claims.title: Galloping merge crossover
claims.hypothesis: Exponential-plus-binary galloping can reduce comparison/control work when one run wins in long streaks but can add overhead on interleaved runs; the best activation threshold is workload- and environment-dependent.
required_evidence: gallop threshold selected on training trials only
held-out comparison against linear merging under the same buffer policy
